**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The licence grant in § 13 sits at the **preferred** position for this rule:

- **§ 13.1** — subscription grant runs to "Customer, its **Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf**," worldwide and non-exclusive, with Authorized User sublicensing. No written-notice gate, so this exceeds the fallback.
- **§ 13.2** — paid-up software and Vendor Technology (including material embedded in a Deliverable) is licensed **perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, fully paid** to Customer and its Affiliates, with modification/derivative rights and contractor support.
- **§ 13.3** — **transferable to an Affiliate or successor** via the Section 24 assignment rights (which permit assignment to an M&A successor without consent), and revocation/suspension is limited to a **material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a reasonable cure opportunity** — no revocation at Vendor's discretion.
- **§ 13.4** restrictions are customary and expressly carved back for legally protected reverse engineering, authorized security testing, and Customer Data/output.

Noted in the rationale but not flagged under this rule: § 14.2 grants only a "revocable, non-transferable" licence to Deliverables for the Order Form term. That language is tempered by § 13.3 (no revocation absent uncured material breach; transfer to Affiliate/successor permitted) and § 14.3 (embedded Vendor Technology takes the § 13.2 perpetual licence). The Deliverable ownership and scope problem belongs to the IP rule, so I have not double-flagged the same commercial term here.
